The American Heritage river cruise paddleboat is seen on its side after being struck by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker ship in the Mississippi River, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, in New Orleans.
Gerald Herbert/AP
hide caption

Gerald Herbert/AP
New Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit against the owner and operator of the tanker that crashed into a docked cruise ship in the Mississippi River on Friday.
The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans is seeking at least $1 million in damages from people connected to the tanker, which is called Atlantic Asphalt. The lawsuit also names the tanker's owner, Nave Shipping SA and its management company Thome Ship Management as defendants.
The lawsuit states that at 12:30 p.m. Friday, the Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashed into the American Heritage river cruise paddleboat which was docked at the Thalia Street terminal for disembarkment of passengers.

item.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
item.description:
Education
A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
November 15, 20265:00 AM ET
Jonaki Mehta
Andrew Pilkington, Siena Rafter, Charlie Rush-Reese, Dylan O'Brien, Roberta Colindrez, Ruth Madeley and Madeline Delp in Being Heumann, premiering November 13, 2026 on Apple TV.
Apple TV
hide caption
toggle caption i
Apple TV
Judy Heumann is known as the mother of the disability rights movement — yet she is lesser known than many of the other civil rights activists of her time. Now, a new film seeks to change that.
Being Heumann, the latest movie from Oscar-winning director Sian Heder, tells the story of the young woman from Brooklyn who led the movement to win the first civil rights protections in the country for people with disabilities.
Before the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) was passed in 1990, there was Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973. It was a single sentence, written into the law, promising people with disabilities the right to fair employment and access to public life without facing discrimination.
But for years, there were no rules or regulations making the federal government actually enforce those protections.

item.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
item.description:
US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
November 14, 20265:15 PM ET
From
By
Amy Maxmen
Anna Fajardo, a public health nurse, offers vaccines at a school registration event in southwestern Utah.
Amy Maxmen/KFF Health News
hide caption
toggle caption i
Amy Maxmen/KFF Health News
The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health triumph secured a quarter century ago.
Researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations on the country's status told KFF Health News that the Pan American Health Organization reached the conclusion this week: Measles has reestablished regular transmission in the country.
PAHO had planned a public announcement on Nov. 17.
In public health parlance, measles elimination depends on a country's sporadic outbreaks ending within a year. That's no longer happening in the United States.
"It's a very sad moment," said Anne Schuchat, an epidemiologist and a former deputy director at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention who was not involved in PAHO's decision.
"Measles causes so much unnecessary suffering, everything from a high fever and missed work and school to long-term complications like progressive degenerative nerve disease and death," Schuchat said. ...
